Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the parking lot collision in
Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you my details in writing if that's alright. I'm still pretty sore and I don't want to get anything
wrong.
Q: That's understandable. We can keep this brief. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in the lot at a grocery store, driving slowly toward an open space near the front row. It was late afternoon and
the lot was pretty busy.
Q: What happened next?
A: A pickup backed out of a space on my right without stopping. I hit the brakes but he still clipped the rear quarter
panel of my car. It wasn't a huge impact, but it jolted me forward and then back against the seat.
Q: Did you notice any injuries right away?
A: Not really at first. I got out, looked at the car, and felt fine enough to drive home. By that night my lower back was
tight, and by the next morning I could barely turn to get out of bed.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider about the back strain?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day. They diagnosed a lumbar strain and told me to rest, take
anti-inflammatories, and do some gentle stretching. I'm still having troulbe sitting for long periods.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add about the collision?
A: Only that I was belted and I was not using my phone. I just want the repairs handled and my back to get better.
Q: Thank you. We will follow up with you in writing about next steps.
A: Okay, thanks.
</page>
